title: Sharabhanga waits for Rama
hook: an old sage makes heaven wait for one look at Rama, which is why Hindus still line up for darshan
carry: darshan: one sight of god outweighs heaven

segments.voice: Yesterday: the atman is never the curse it wears. Viradha rose free from the pit, a cursed musician released, and sent the brothers to a sage.

Rama follows Viradha's directions, and near Sharabhanga's hermitage he stops. There's a chariot in the air above the clearing, blazing like the sun, pulled by green horses. A white umbrella shades the figure in it, and attendants crowd around. That's Indra, Rama tells Lakshmana, king of the gods, talking with the sage. And as the brothers walk closer, Indra says something to his companions, and the chariot rises and goes.
screen: `A CHARIOT ABOVE THE CLEARING.` → `INDRA, KING OF THE GODS.` → `HE LEAVES AS RAMA COMES.`

segments.voice: Why does Indra leave? Valmiki gives his reason: Rama has a great task ahead, and Indra will meet him only once it's done. The text hints at a war the gods need Rama to fight, but says no more. Picture it anyway: the king of the gods stepping aside for a man in bark clothes. Rama goes in, and the very old sage welcomes him. Indra came to take me to Brahma's world, Sharabhanga says. I've earned it by my tapas. But I heard you were near, and I wouldn't go until I had seen you, my guest. Think about that. Heaven is waiting at the door, and he makes it wait, for one look at Rama. For devotees, Rama is Vishnu himself, and this is darshan: seeing God, and being seen. It's why Hindus go to the temple even with a shrine at home. You stand in line, the curtain opens, and for a few seconds you look at the murti and the murti looks back at you. Many say that moment is the point of the whole visit. Then the sage offers Rama all the worlds his tapas has won. Rama declines, kindly. I'll earn my own worlds. Just tell me where to live. Sharabhanga points him to another sage, Sutikshna. But first he asks Rama to stay and watch. He has one last thing to do.
screen: `I SHOULDN'T MEET HIM YET.` · `I WAITED TO SEE YOU.` · `DARSHAN: TO SEE AND BE SEEN.` · `THE MURTI LOOKS BACK.` · then, large: `ONE LOOK, OVER HEAVEN.`

segments.voice: Hindus can take darshan in the mind, too. Close your eyes and picture the face of the form of God you know best, Rama, Krishna, Ganesha, the Goddess, the way it looks when the temple curtain opens. If you pray, just look, and let yourself be looked at, as you breathe. If you don't, picture a face that has looked at you with love, and rest in being seen.
Sharabhanga. The old sage who made heaven wait so he could see Rama, then offered him all his merit, which Rama kindly declined.
Your line: darshan: one sight of God outweighs heaven. Sharabhanga made heaven wait for it. See you tomorrow.

howItsDone: In the text, Indra withdraws before meeting Rama, and some devotees read the scene as the gods waiting on Rama's mission.
